CHEMISTRY — TERMLY EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Water always increases oxygen

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.

4. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

6. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 50 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.

8. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.

10. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Iron rusting

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.

14. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non-metals ● Sources of selected non- metals , ● General methods of gas collecti.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
